details.sortie: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. They are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood.

Everyone is entitled to all the rights and freedoms set forth in this Declaration, without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status. Furthermore, no distinction shall be made on the basis of the status of the country or territory, whether it is independent, under the authority of the United Nations, non-self-governing, or subject to any limitation upon its sovereignty.
Every individual has the right to life, liberty, and security of person.
No one shall be held in slavery or servitude; slavery and the slave trade are prohibited in all their forms.
No one shall be subjected to torture, or to inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.
Everyone has the right to recognition everywhere of their legal personality.

All are equal before the law and have, without distinction, the right to equal protection of the law. All have the right to equal protection against any discrimination that would violate the present Declaration and against any incitement to such discrimination.
Every person has the right to an effective remedy before national competent authorities for acts violating fundamental rights recognized to them by the constitution or by law.
No one shall be arbitrarily arrested, detained, or exiled.

Every person has the right, without any discrimination, to have his or her matter heard equitably and publicly by an independent and impartial tribunal which will decide, in a public hearing, on his or her rights and obligations, or on the merits of any criminal charge against him or her.

Any person accused of an offense is presumed innocent until proven guilty according to law in a public trial where all necessary guarantees for their defense have been assured. No one shall be convicted for acts or omissions that, at the time they were committed, did not constitute an offense under national or international law. Furthermore, no punishment shall be inflicted that is more severe than that which was applicable at the time the offense was committed.

No one shall be subject to arbitrary interference with his or her privacy, family, home or correspondence, nor to attacks upon his or her honour and reputation. Everyone has the right to the protection of the law against such interference or attacks.
Every person has the right to move freely and to choose their residence within a State. Every person has the right to leave any country, including their own, and to return to their country.

In the face of persecution, every person has the right to seek asylum and to benefit from asylum in other countries. This right cannot be invoked in the case of proceedings genuinely based on a common criminal offense or conduct contrary to the purposes and principles of the United Nations.
Every individual has the right to nationality. No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his nationality or the right to change his nationality.

From the age of maturity, men and women, without any restriction as to race, nationality, or religion, have the right to marry and found a family. They have equal rights regarding marriage, during marriage, and upon its dissolution. Marriage shall be entered into only with the free and full consent of the intending spouses. The family is the natural and fundamental unit of society and is entitled to protection by the society and the State.
Every person, whether acting alone or in community, has the right to property. No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of their property.

Every person has the right to freedom of thought, conscience, and religion; this right includes freedom to change their religion or belief, and freedom to manifest their religion or belief, either individually or in community with others, and in public or in private, by teaching, practice, worship, and observance.

Every individual has the right to freedom of opinion and expression, which implies the right to hold opinions without interference and to seek, receive and impart information and ideas through any media without borders.
Every person has the right to the freedom of peaceful assembly and association. No one can be forced to join an association.

Every person has the right to take part in the conduct of public affairs of his country, either directly or through freely chosen representatives. Every person has the right to access, on an equal basis, the public offices of his country. The will of the people constitutes the basis of the authority of public powers; this will must be expressed through honest elections which must take place periodically, by universal and equal suffrage and by secret ballot or by another equivalent procedure ensuring the freedom of vote.

Every person, as a member of society, has the right to social security; she is entitled to the fulfillment of the economic, social, and cultural rights essential to her dignity and the free development of her personality, through national effort and international cooperation, taking into account the organization and resources of each country.

Every person has the right to work, to free choice of employment, to just and favourable conditions of work and to protection against unemployment. All have the right to equal pay for equal work without any discrimination. Anyone who works has the right to reasonable remuneration ensuring him and his family an existence worthy of human dignity, social and medical insurance, and other means of protection against risk. Every person has the right to form trade unions for the protection of his interests.
Every person has the right to rest and leisure, and in particular to reasonable limitation of working hours and periodic paid leave.

Every person has the right to a standard of living adequate for the health and well-being of himself or herself and of his or her family, including food, clothing, housing, medical care and necessary social services; he or she also has the right to security in the event of unemployment, sickness, disability, widowhood, old age, or other lack of livelihood in circumstances beyond his or her control. Motherhood and childhood are entitled to special care and assistance. All children, whether born in or out of marriage, shall enjoy the same social security.

Everyone has the right to education. Education shall be free, at least in the case of elementary and secondary education. Elementary education shall be compulsory. Technical and vocational education shall be generally available and directed to meeting the needs of the community. Higher education shall be equally accessible to all on the basis of merit. Education shall aim at the full development of the human personality and the strengthening of respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. It shall promote understanding, tolerance and friendship among all nations, racial or religious groups, and shall further the activities of the United Nations for the maintenance of peace. Parents have, without discrimination of any kind, the primary responsibility for the upbringing and development of their children, and they have the right to choose the kind of education that shall be given to their children.

Every person has the right to freely participate in the cultural life of the community, to enjoy the arts, and to participate in scientific progress and in its benefits. Everyone has the right to the protection of the moral and material interests resulting from any scientific, literary, or artistic production of which he is the author.
Every person has the right that, on the social and international planes, there prevail an order in which the rights and freedoms set forth in this Declaration can be fully realized.

The individual has duties towards the community in which alone the free and full development of his personality is possible. In the exercise of his rights and the enjoyment of his freedoms, everyone shall be subject only to such limitations as are determined by law solely for the purpose of securing due recognition and respect for the rights and freedoms of others and of meeting the just requirements of morality, public order, and the general welfare in a democratic society. These rights and freedoms may in no case be exercised contrary to the purposes and principles of the United Nations.

No provision of the present Declaration shall be interpreted as implying for any State, group or individual any right to engage in any activity or perform any act aimed at the destruction of the rights and freedoms set forth herein.
